when.quote: If any fees on the customer's account do not match the correct amounts per the documented fee schedule, the agent must identify all fee discrepancies and apply a credit for the net correction.

starts.note: customer: start only when the customer asks for a review of fees or rebates on their checking accounts. The agent does not offer credits unprompted. Once the review shows a discrepancy, the agent must explain it and offer the correction. It applies the credit after the customer agrees.
starts.quote: Simply contact us, and we'll thoroughly review the charge in question. If we determine that the fee was applied in error, we'll promptly credit your account for the full amount.

info.about: Any 2 of: date of birth, email, phone number, address, plus a name, email or user id so the agent can look up the record
info.ask: To verify your identity, could you give me your full name and two of these: date of birth, email, phone number, or address?

info.about: Which checking account(s) the customer thinks have wrong fees
info.ask: Which of your checking accounts are the fees on?

info.about: The month or statement cycle the customer wants reviewed
info.ask: Which month or statement period should I review?

info.about: What looks wrong: a fee type (ATM, monthly maintenance and so on) or a missing rebate. The customer may not know. If so, the agent reviews every fee in the period
info.ask: Which fees or rebates look wrong to you? If you aren't sure, I can review every fee in that period.

info.about: account_id, account_class (product name such as Blue Account, Green Account (checking), Bluest Account or Light Green Account), account_type, status and balance of each account

atm_withdrawal, atm_fee, monthly_fee, fee_rebate, rebate_credit and fee_refund transactions in the review period. Include their descriptions (in-network, domestic out-of-network or foreign) and the withdrawal amounts
Used to confirm Light Green Account age eligibility (13–24)
Whether the customer wants the identified corrections credited
info.ask: I found fees that don't match your account's fee schedule. Would you like me to credit the difference back to each affected account?

steps.do: Greet the customer and ask what they need. Ask which accounts, which review period and what looks wrong, if they have not said. Ask for identity details. Share no account data yet
steps.quote: Verify the customer's identity and account ownership

steps.do: Look up the customer's record by the name, email or id they gave

args.customer_name: the name the customer gave (or use get_user_information_by_email / _by_id)

steps.quote: 1. Verify the customer's identity and account ownership

steps.do: Confirm that at least 2 of DOB, email, phone and address match the record. Do not reveal any account data before this. If fewer than 2 match, ask again. If they still do not match, tell the customer you cannot verify them and stop
steps.quote: 1. Verify the customer's identity and account ownership

steps.do: Get the current time for the verification log
steps.quote: 1. Verify the customer's identity and account ownership

steps.do: Log the verification
steps.quote: 1. Verify the customer's identity and account ownership

steps.do: Unlock the account lookup tool
steps.quote: Use get_all_user_accounts_by_user_id_3847 to retrieve the bank accounts (checkings, savings) for a customer.

steps.do: Get all the customer's accounts. Confirm each disputed account is a checking account they own, and note its account_class
steps.quote: 2. Confirm the account is a checking account (credits cannot be applied to savings or other account types)

steps.do: If an account the customer named is not in get_accounts, tell them. If it is not a checking account, explain that this credit applies only to checking accounts and do not credit it here
steps.if: an account in question is missing from the records or is not a checking account
steps.quote: Credits may ONLY be applied to checking accounts. Savings accounts and other account types are not eligible.

steps.do: Unlock the transaction history tool
steps.quote: Agents can retrieve the transaction history for a customer's bank account (checking or savings) using the get_bank_account_transactions_9173 tool.

steps.do: Get the transaction history for each checking account in question. If the customer is unsure which account, get it for every checking account they name. Results come newest first

arguments.account_id: each checking account id in question, from get_accounts

steps.quote: - Check the transaction history to confirm each fee discrepancy

steps.do: For a Bluest Account in the review period, the correct fees are $2.00 per domestic out-of-network withdrawal and a $0.00 Rho-Bank fee per foreign ATM withdrawal. Overcharge = posted ATM fees minus correct fees. Also check whether ATM fee rebates owed (up to $50 per month) are missing from the fee_rebate entries
steps.quote: Single withdrawal: Withdrawing cash once from an out-of-network ATM will incur a fee of $2.00, plus any ATM operator surcharge.

steps.do: For a Light Green Account in the review period, the first 4 domestic out-of-network withdrawals in the month are free (count them in date order), and each one after that costs $1.50. Foreign withdrawals are charged by tier, per withdrawal: $2.00 up to and including $100, $3.50 above $100 up to and including $300, $5.00 above $300. Overcharge = posted ATM fees minus correct fees
steps.quote: You get 4 free out-of-network ATM withdrawals per month before the $1.50 fee applies.

steps.do: For a Blue Account in the review period, pair each ATM withdrawal with its atm_fee. Domestic out-of-network fee = 1% of the withdrawal, capped at $3.00 each. Foreign-currency fee = the greater of 3% of the USD amount or $5.00 each. In-network fee = $0. Overcharge = posted ATM fees minus correct fees. An undercharge is negative
steps.quote: Out-of-network ATM withdrawal: 1% of withdrawal amount (max $3.00)

steps.do: For a Green Account (checking) in the review period, pair each ATM withdrawal with its atm_fee. Domestic out-of-network fee = flat $3.00 each. Foreign fee = the greater of 3% of the USD-equivalent amount or $5.00 each. Overcharge = posted ATM fees minus correct fees. An undercharge is negative
steps.quote: Withdrawals at non-network ATMs incur a fee of $3.00 per transaction.

steps.do: For any other checking product, search the knowledge base for its own at-a-glance, fee and ATM documents. Work out each correct fee and any promised rebate from them before judging. Check other fee lines (monthly_fee and so on) against the product's schedule the same way
steps.if: account_class is not covered by a compute_ step above, or fees other than ATM fees are in question
steps.quote: Review the account terms and documented fee structures to identify all fees that differ from what should have been charged

steps.do: For each account, net correction = sum of overcharges − undercharges + missing rebates − any refunds or rebates already posted for the same fees. Use exact cents and do not round. Choose credit_type: fee_refund for wrongly charged fees, rebate_credit for missing rebates. If both apply, use the type that covers the majority of the corrections
steps.quote: Ensure the credit amount reflects the net correction across all identified fee discrepancies

steps.do: If an account's net correction is 0 or less, tell the customer its fees match the documented schedule and explain how they are calculated. Apply no credit to that account. Do not credit for any other reason, because that needs supervisor approval
steps.if: net correction for an account is not greater than 0
steps.quote: Credits may only be applied for the two circumstances listed above. Do not apply credits for any other reason without supervisor approval.

steps.do: Tell the customer which fees were wrong and by how much on each account, then offer to apply a credit
steps.quote: 3. Verify the customer meets one of the eligible circumstances listed above

steps.do: Unlock the checking credit tool
steps.if: at least one account has a net correction greater than 0 and the customer accepted the offer
steps.quote: The apply_checking_account_credit_5829 tool is used to add a credit transaction to a checking account.

steps.do: Apply ONE credit per account for that account's exact net correction (fee overcharges and any missing rebates combined)

arguments.account_id: the checking account id from get_accounts
arguments.amount: exact net correction for that account from compute_net
arguments.credit_type: fee_refund (or rebate_credit if missing rebates are the majority of the correction)

steps.if: net correction for that account is greater than 0 and the customer agreed; repeat once for each such account
steps.quote: Because only one credit call is allowed per account, if multiple corrections are needed for the same account (e.g., both fee refunds and missing rebates), combine them into a single credit with the total amount and use the credit_type that applies to the majority of the corrections.

steps.do: If the credit call returns an error (for example, the 14-day cooldown after an earlier credit), do not retry it and do not credit another account instead. Explain that the credit cannot be applied now and ask whether the customer wants a human agent. Transfer only if they agree

args.summary: the review done, the discrepancies found and the error returned
args.reason: checking credit could not be applied

steps.if: apply_checking_account_credit_5829 returned an error and the customer agrees to a transfer
steps.quote: After a credit is applied to a checking account, the system enforces a 14-day cooldown period before another credit can be applied to that same account.

steps.do: Using the credit results, tell the customer the credit applied to each account and its new balance. Tell them they do not need to do anything else. Mention that in-network ATMs avoid out-of-network fees
steps.quote: 6. Inform the customer of the applied credit and new account balance

rules.rule: Credits may be applied only to checking accounts, and only for missing rebates or fee mischarges
rules.quote: Credits may only be applied for the two circumstances listed above. Do not apply credits for any other reason without supervisor approval.

rules.rule: Call apply_checking_account_credit_5829 at most once per checking account per interaction
rules.quote: The apply_checking_account_credit_5829 tool may only be called ONCE per checking account per customer interaction.

rules.rule: The credit equals the exact net correction across all fee discrepancies on that account, with no rounding
rules.quote: The credit amount must match the exact rebate or fee amount - do not round or estimate.

rules.rule: Find every fee discrepancy on the account, not just the ones the customer named
rules.quote: - Ensure the credit amount reflects the net correction across all identified fee discrepancies

rules.rule: Bluest: domestic out-of-network ATM fee is $2.00 per withdrawal
rules.quote: The fee is assessed per withdrawal. Multiple withdrawals will each incur a separate fee.

rules.rule: Bluest: the Rho-Bank foreign ATM withdrawal fee is $0.00, so any Rho foreign ATM fee is a mischarge
rules.quote: Withdraw from ATMs abroad with no Rho-Bank fee: $0.00. Third-party ATM operator fees may still apply.

rules.rule: Bluest: ATM fee rebates are capped at $50 per month
rules.quote: If your aggregate ATM fees exceed $50 in a given month, the excess will not be rebated.

rules.rule: Bluest: rebates cover third-party ATM fees
rules.quote: When you incur third-party ATM fees, you are rebated up to $50 per monthly statement cycle.

rules.rule: Before crediting a missing rebate, confirm it was not already applied
rules.quote: - Confirm the rebate has not already been applied by checking the account's transaction history

rules.rule: Light Green: 4 free domestic out-of-network withdrawals per month, then $1.50 each
rules.quote: You get 4 free out-of-network ATM withdrawals per month before the $1.50 fee applies.

rules.rule: Light Green foreign ATM fee is set by tier for each withdrawal: <=$100 → $2.00; >$100 and <=$300 → $3.50; >$300 → $5.00. An amount exactly at a threshold gets the lower tier's fee
rules.quote: Amounts exactly at a threshold are charged the lower tier’s fee.

rules.rule: Light Green foreign ATM fees are flat for each withdrawal and depend on that single withdrawal's amount
rules.quote: Foreign ATM withdrawal fees on Light Green accounts are flat per withdrawal and depend on the amount you take out in a single transaction.

rules.rule: Light Green holder must be 13–24
rules.quote: You must be the primary account holder and be between 13 and 24 years old to open the account.

rules.rule: Blue Account: domestic out-of-network ATM fee = 1% of the withdrawal, at most $3.00 per withdrawal
rules.quote: Out-of-network ATM withdrawal: 1% of withdrawal amount (max $3.00)

rules.rule: Blue Account: foreign-currency ATM fee = the greater of 3% of the withdrawal or $5.00, per withdrawal
rules.quote: For ATM withdrawals made in a foreign currency, you are charged 3% of the withdrawal amount, with a minimum fee of $5.00 per withdrawal.

rules.rule: Blue Account: in-network ATMs carry no out-of-network fee
rules.quote: Use in-network ATMs to avoid out-of-network ATM fees

rules.rule: Green Account (checking): domestic out-of-network ATM fee is a flat $3.00 per withdrawal. ATM-owner surcharges are separate
rules.quote: Withdrawals at non-network ATMs incur a fee of $3.00 per transaction.

rules.rule: Green Account (checking): foreign ATM fee = the greater of 3% of the USD-equivalent amount or $5.00, per withdrawal
rules.quote: Compare the result to $5.00. The higher amount is your fee.

rules.rule: A 14-day cooldown follows any credit to the same checking account
rules.quote: After a credit is applied to a checking account, the system enforces a 14-day cooldown period before another credit can be applied to that same account.

rules.rule: credit_type is 'fee_refund' for wrongly charged fees and 'rebate_credit' for missing rebates
rules.quote: For refunding fees that were incorrectly charged

done_when: The customer is verified and logged. Every fee and rebate in the review period on each checking account in question has been checked against its product's documented fee schedule. Exactly one credit has been applied to each account with a positive net correction, after the customer agreed. The customer has been told each credited amount and new balance, or why no credit applies, or why the credit failed (with a transfer offered).
